info.title: Tackle Co-Sell for AWS Partner Central
info.description:
This API lets you create and manage co-sell opportunities and invitations
in AWS Partner Central — formerly known as the AWS Partner Network Customer
Engagement (ACE) program. Use it to share opportunities you originate
(Partner Referrals) with AWS, and to receive, respond to, and manage
opportunities and invitations that AWS originates (AWS Referrals) for
your account.

## Authentication

This API requires a Tackle machine-to-machine (MTM) access token. Issue
your M2M client credentials following the [How to get an M2M client ID
and secret](https://developers.tackle.io/docs/how-to-get-an-m2m-client-id-and-secret)
guide, exchange them for an access token following the [Getting an
access token](https://developers.tackle.io/docs/getting-an-access-token)
guide, then send the token with each request in the `Authorization`
header as `Bearer <access_token>`.

The MTM token supplies the vendor and organization context for the request.
Fine-grained scoped MTM permissions are not enforced for this API yet.

## Pagination

`listOpportunities`, `listInvitations`, and `listSolutions` use offset-based
pagination. Set `pageSize` (1–100, default 10) and either omit `from` to
start from the first record or set `from` to the value returned in
`nextIndex` from the previous page's response. The response's `isNextPage`
indicates whether more results are available; `nextIndex` is only present
when `isNextPage` is `true`.

`listOpportunityEvents` and `listInvitationEvents` use cursor-based
pagination via the `next` query parameter. The response schema includes a
`next` cursor field reserved for future use; today no cursor value is
emitted, so a single response returns the full event history for the
requested entity.

## Errors

Most 4xx and 5xx responses use the `Error` envelope (a JSON object with a
human-readable `message`). Some responses are returned as empty bodies
(typically direct `Unauthorized` and `Internal Server Error` responses) —
clients should be tolerant of an empty body and treat the HTTP status code
as authoritative.

## Related Tackle Co-Sell APIs

Tackle publishes equivalent Co-Sell APIs for other cloud providers. Customer
engagement domain models differ across providers (AWS and Google Cloud
Channel use "opportunities"; Microsoft Partner Center uses "referrals"), so
endpoint paths, request and response shapes, and pagination details are not
interchangeable.

- Tackle Co-Sell for Google Cloud Channel: https://gcp.cosell.tackle.io
- Tackle Co-Sell for Microsoft Partner Center: https://msft.cosell.tackle.io

tags.name: Opportunities
tags.description:
Create, read, update, and list co-sell opportunities — the partner-
originated (Outbound / Partner Referral) and AWS-originated (Inbound
/ AWS Referral) deals tracked in AWS Partner Central. Includes the
opportunity history endpoint for inspecting cloud-side request and
response detail.

tags.name: Invitations
tags.description:
Create (test-environment-only), read, update, and list co-sell
invitations — AWS-led requests to partner with you on a specific
opportunity. Use the update operation to accept or reject an
invitation, and the history endpoint to inspect cloud-side detail.

tags.name: Solutions
tags.description:
List the co-sell solutions registered with AWS Partner Central for
your account. Solution identifiers are referenced by `solutions` on
opportunities.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A search query to filter the opportunities.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The starting index of the opportunities to return.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of opportunities to return per page (minimum 1, maximum 100, default 10).

parameters.name: cloudStatus
parameters.description:
Filter opportunities by their AWS Partner Central review status. Accepts
multiple values; results match any of the supplied statuses.

Status values:

- `Pending Submission` — opportunity is drafted but has not yet been
  submitted to AWS Partner Central for review.
- `Submitted` — opportunity has been submitted and is awaiting AWS triage.
- `In review` — AWS is actively reviewing the opportunity.
- `Approved` — AWS has approved the opportunity.
- `Rejected` — AWS has rejected the opportunity. See `cloudResponses` on
  the matching opportunity event for the rejection reason.
- `Action Required` — AWS requires updates before the review can proceed.
  See `cloudResponses` on the matching opportunity event for the requested
  changes.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description:
Filter opportunities by their Tackle source. `Inbound` corresponds to
opportunities originated by AWS (AWS Referral); `Outbound` corresponds
to opportunities originated by the partner (Partner Referral). Accepts
multiple values; results match any of the supplied sources.

parameters.name: cloudSalesStage
parameters.description:
Filter opportunities by the AWS Partner Central sales-stage value.
Accepts multiple values; results match any of the supplied stages.
See `lifeCycle.stage` on `Opportunity` for the documented stage values
(for example, `Prospect`, `Qualified`, `Technical Validation`,
`Business Validation`, `Committed`, `Launched`, `Closed Lost`).

parameters.name: startTargetCloseDate
parameters.description: Used to filter opportunities by their target close date. Only opportunities with a target close date on or after this specified date will be retrieved.

parameters.name: endTargetCloseDate
parameters.description: Used to filter opportunities based on their target close date. Only opportunities with a target close date on or before this specified date will be retrieved.

parameters.name: startCloudCreated
parameters.description: Used to filter opportunities by specifying the earliest creation date. Opportunities created on or after this date will be included in the results.

parameters.name: endCloudCreated
parameters.description: Used to filter opportunities by specifying the latest creation date. Opportunities created on or before this date will be included in the results.

parameters.name: sortField
parameters.description:
The field to sort the opportunities by. Only takes effect when `sortOrder`
is also supplied; both query parameters must be present together for sorting
to apply. If only `sortField` is provided, the response uses the default
ordering instead. Note that `cloudProviderID` is case-sensitive: the trailing
`ID` is uppercase, and sending `cloudProviderId` (lowercase `d`) returns
`400 Bad Request: Invalid sortField`.

parameters.name: sortOrder
parameters.description:
Sort direction. Only takes effect when `sortField` is also supplied — both
query parameters must be present together. If only `sortOrder` is provided
(without `sortField`), the response uses the underlying default ordering
instead of any sort. There is no implicit ascending default applied when
only one of the two parameters is sent.

parameters.name: crmId
parameters.description:
Filter by the Salesforce CRM identifier of the linked opportunity record.
For Salesforce, both 15- and 18-character IDs are accepted. To filter by
a HubSpot Deal ID instead, see the `hubspotCrmId` field on
`OpportunityMetadata`.

parameters.name: hasCloudErrors
parameters.description:
Filter opportunities by their AWS Partner Central error state. Set to
`true` to return only opportunities whose most recent AWS Partner Central
request failed; set to `false` to return only opportunities with no
cloud-side errors. Omit to disable the filter. Inspect
`listOpportunityEvents` for the matching opportunity to see the error
detail.

parameters.name: hasCrmId
parameters.description:
Filter opportunities by whether a CRM identifier is linked. Set to `true`
to return only opportunities that have a `crmId` (Salesforce) or
`hubspotCrmId` value populated; set to `false` to return only
opportunities with no CRM identifier linked. Omit to disable the filter.

parameters.name: hasSalesforceErrors
parameters.description:
Filter opportunities by their Salesforce sync state. Set to `true` to
return only opportunities whose most recent Salesforce sync attempt
failed; set to `false` to return only opportunities with no Salesforce
sync errors. Omit to disable the filter. The error message itself is
available on the matching opportunity in the `salesforceSyncError` field.

parameters.name: hasAnyError
parameters.description:
Filters opportunities by their error state.

- `true` returns only opportunities that currently have at least one
  cloud-side error or Salesforce-sync error.
- `false` returns only opportunities that have no cloud-side or
  Salesforce-sync errors.
- Omit the parameter to disable this filter entirely.

See `hasCloudErrors` and `hasSalesforceErrors` to filter on each error
source independently.

post.description:
Queues a create request against AWS Partner Central. The success response is `202 Accepted`
with the Tackle identifier; poll `getOpportunity` to observe the cloud-side outcome.

If a `crmId` is supplied and your vendor account enforces a one-opportunity-per-CRM-ID
constraint, the request is rejected with `409 Conflict` when an existing co-sell
opportunity already maps to the same CRM identifier. Whether this constraint is enforced
is configured per vendor; contact your Tackle account team if you need to change the
behavior.

schema.description:
Selects the create flow. `createOpportunity` (the default) creates the
opportunity and starts the AWS engagement; `createDraftOpportunity` creates
the opportunity in draft state without starting an engagement.

Header matching is lenient: only `createDraftOpportunity` is matched
explicitly, and any other value (including unknown values, an empty
string, or an omitted header) is routed through the default
`createOpportunity` flow rather than rejected with `400 Bad Request`.
Clients should still send one of the documented values so future
server-side validation can be adopted without a breaking change.

salesActivities: Customer has shown interest in solution

202.description:
Accepted. The create-opportunity request has been queued for asynchronous processing
in AWS Partner Central. The returned `id` is the Tackle identifier that can be used
immediately with `getOpportunity` and `updateOpportunity`; the cloud-side identifier
(`cloudProviderId`) becomes available once the request reaches AWS.

id.description: The Tackle identifier for the opportunity.

200.description:
OK. When the cloud-side payload is unavailable for the opportunity (for example,
immediately after `createOpportunity` returns 202 but before AWS Partner Central
has populated the cloud-side record), the response may contain only `metadata` and
omit `awsOpportunitySummary`, `customer`, `lifeCycle`, and the other AWS-derived
fields. Clients should treat fields outside `metadata` as optional.

getOpportunity.description: You can retrieve the opportunity information by providing the unique identifier for the opportunity.

project.customerBusinessProblem: An example business problem that needs solving
salesActivities: Customer has shown interest in solution
project.title: Test opportunity

post.description:
Queues a partial update against AWS Partner Central. The exact behavior depends on
the value of the `tackle-operation-id` header.

- Production cloud operations: `updateOpportunity` (default), `updateDraftOpportunity`,
  `updateStartEngagementOpportunity`, `startEngagement`, `closeLostOpportunity`,
  `launchOpportunity`, `updateOpportunityCRMID`.
- Test-environment-only: `acceptOpportunity`, `rejectOpportunity`. These simulate
  AWS-side responses to an incoming engagement invitation/opportunity and are routable
  only for vendor accounts provisioned for use in a test environment. Production vendor
  accounts that send one of these operation IDs receive `400 Bad Request` with the
  message `the requested operation is only supported in test or demo environments.`

The success response is `202 Accepted` with an empty body; poll `getOpportunity` or
`listOpportunityEvents` to observe the outcome of the queued request.

schema.description:
Selects the operation to perform. The values `acceptOpportunity` and
`rejectOpportunity` are test-environment-only and return `400 Bad Request`
for production vendors with the message
`the requested operation is only supported in test or demo environments.`

updateOpportunity.description: You will likely want to update the opportunity information at some point during the process, to do so you will need to include the `updateOpportunity` operation ID in the header.

updateStartEngagementOpportunity.summary: Update and start engagement for the opportunity
updateStartEngagementOpportunity.description: You will likely want to update and start engaging a draft opportunity at some point during the process, to do so you will need to include the `updateStartEngagementOpportunity` tackle-operation-id in the header.

startEngagement.summary: Start engagement for a draft opportunity
startEngagement.description: When you are ready to start engaging with AWS, you will need to include the `startEngagement` operation ID in the header.

closeLostOpportunity.description: If the opportunity is no longer viable, you can close it as lost. To do so, you will need to include the `closeLostOpportunity` operation ID in the header.

launchOpportunity.description: When the opportunity is ready to be launched, you will need to include the `launchOpportunity` operation ID in the header.

updateOpportunityCRMID.summary: Sets the crmID for the opportunity and a linked invitation if it exists
updateOpportunityCRMID.description: A user can set a crmID on an opportunity after the user created the opportunity. This is useful when the user wants to link the opportunity to a CRM record (e.g. Salesforce opportunity record).

acceptOpportunity.description:
Test-environment-only. Simulates AWS accepting an incoming opportunity
so that downstream workflows can be exercised without sending the
request to AWS Partner Central. The request body is ignored. Production
vendors that send `acceptOpportunity` receive `400 Bad Request` with the
message `the requested operation is only supported in test or demo environments.`

rejectOpportunity.description:
Test-environment-only. Simulates AWS rejecting an incoming opportunity
so that downstream workflows can be exercised without sending the
request to AWS Partner Central. The request body is ignored. Production
vendors that send `rejectOpportunity` receive `400 Bad Request` with the
message `the requested operation is only supported in test or demo environments.`

202.description:
Accepted. The update request has been queued for asynchronous processing in AWS
Partner Central. The response body is empty; poll `getOpportunity` or
`listOpportunityEvents` to observe the result of the queued request.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description:
Cursor token used to resume a paginated history query. When supplied, the
query continues from where a previous request left off.

**Note**: this endpoint does not currently emit `next` cursors on responses
(see the `next` field of the response schema below), so in practice clients
have no way to obtain a cursor from the API itself today. This parameter is
therefore rarely useful unless a cursor value is already known from another
source.

next.description:
Reserved cursor for the next page of history events.
**This endpoint does not currently emit this field** — no
cursor is produced today, so the field is always omitted
from the JSON response. Treat this field as reserved for
a future paginated response; do not rely on its absence
to detect end-of-data today, and do not depend on it
appearing in responses.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A search query to filter the invitations.

parameters.name: cloudStatus
parameters.description:
Filter invitations by their AWS Partner Central status. Accepts multiple
values; results match any of the supplied statuses. Common values include
`PENDING`, `ACCEPTED`, `REJECTED`, and `EXPIRED` — see the `status` field
on `InvitationResponse` for the full list of values returned by the API.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of invitations to return per page (minimum 1, maximum 100, default 10).

parameters.name: crmId
parameters.description:
Filter by the Salesforce CRM identifier of the linked opportunity record.
For Salesforce, both 15- and 18-character IDs are accepted. To filter by
a HubSpot Deal ID instead, see the `hubspotCrmId` field on
`OpportunityMetadata`.

parameters.name: opportunityId
parameters.description:
Filter invitations by the AWS Partner Central opportunity identifier
(for example, `O1234123`) of the opportunity an invitation is linked to.
This is the cloud-provider identifier, not the Tackle identifier — to
look up an invitation by Tackle ID, use the path-level `getInvitation`
operation instead.

parameters.name: origin
parameters.description:
Filter invitations by who initiated them. Use `aws` to return only AWS-led
invitations (AWS reaching out to your account about an opportunity), and
`partner` to return only partner-led invitations (your account reaching
out to AWS).

parameters.name: endCloudCreated

post.description:
Creates a simulated invitation for exercising invitation workflows in a
test environment. This endpoint is only available to vendor accounts
provisioned for use in a test environment; production vendor accounts
receive `403 Forbidden`.

schema.description:
Reserved for forward compatibility. This header is not currently inspected
for `createInvitation`; the value is ignored at the API gateway today and any
value is accepted. Clients are encouraged to send `createInvitation` so that
future server-side validation can be adopted without a breaking change.

createInvitation.description: Create a new invitation to use in test environments

invitationID.description:
The Tackle ID for the created invitation. Note: this field is
emitted as `invitationID` (capital `ID`) by `createInvitation`,
while `getInvitation` returns the same logical value as
`invitationId` (lowercase `d`). Consumers should handle both.

id.description: The simulated AWS engagement-invitation identifier assigned in the test environment.

arn.description: The simulated Amazon Resource Name (ARN) for the engagement invitation in the test environment.

403.description:
Forbidden. Production vendors that call `createInvitation` receive this
response. Unlike most error responses on this API, this 403 response is
returned as plain text (`Forbidden`) with `Content-Type: text/plain` rather
than the `Error` JSON envelope used elsewhere. Clients should not attempt
to JSON-decode this 403 body.

parameters.name: invitation_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the invitation

getInvitation.description: You can retrieve the invitation information by providing the unique identifier for the invitation.

project.title: Cloud Migration Project
project.businessProblem: Customer needs to migrate three legacy datacenter workloads to AWS to reduce operational overhead and improve disaster-recovery posture.

parameters.name: invitation_id
parameters.description: The unique identifier for the invitation

schema.description: The unique identifier for the update operation

requestBody.description:
Body shape depends on the `tackle-operation-id` header. The body is parsed
differently for each operation: `acceptInvitation` reads only `crmId`, and
`rejectInvitation` reads only `rejectionReason`. Each property is optional at
the schema level and only meaningful for the matching operation; properties
for the other operation are ignored.

**Body requirement by operation**:

- For `acceptInvitation`, the request body is fully optional. An empty body,
  `{}`, or `{"crmId": "..."}` are all accepted; an empty body skips body
  parsing entirely.
- For `rejectInvitation`, the request body must be a present, non-empty JSON
  object — at minimum `{}`. An empty (zero-length) body fails to parse and
  surfaces as a `500 Internal Server Error`, not a `400 Bad Request`. Always
  send at least `{}` (or include `rejectionReason` to propagate a reason to
  AWS Partner Central).

crmId.description:
Salesforce CRM ID for the opportunity that an accepted invitation
should be linked to. Optional, and only meaningful when
`tackle-operation-id` is `acceptInvitation`. If supplied as a
15-character Salesforce ID, it is converted to the canonical
18-character form before being persisted and forwarded to AWS
Partner Central. Ignored on reject-path requests.

rejectionReason.description:
Reason supplied when rejecting an invitation. Optional, and only
meaningful when `tackle-operation-id` is `rejectInvitation`. Ignored on
accept-path requests.

accept.description: When you are ready to accept the invitation, you will need to include the `acceptInvitation` operation ID in the header. You can also send an optional crmId in the body

reject.description: If you are unable to accept the invitation, you can reject it. To do so, you will need to include the `rejectInvitation` operation ID in the header.

202.description:
Accepted. The invitation update has been queued for asynchronous processing in AWS
Partner Central. The response body is empty.

get.description:
Returns the active co-sell solutions registered with AWS Partner Central for the
authenticated vendor.

For vendor accounts provisioned for use in a test environment, this endpoint
returns a fixed three-solution fixture; the `q`, `from`, `pageSize`, and
`all` query parameters are **ignored** for these vendors and the response
body is the same fixture set regardless of what the client sends. Production
vendor accounts receive vendor-specific results that honor every query
parameter.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: A search query to filter the solutions.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The starting index of the solutions to return.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: The number of solutions to return per page (minimum 1, maximum 100, default 10).

parameters.name: all
parameters.description:
Set to `true` to return solutions in any status, including inactive ones.
Defaults to `false` (only active solutions are returned).

bearerAuth.description: Tackle machine-to-machine access token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

opportunity_id.name: opportunity_id
opportunity_id.description:
The Tackle identifier for the opportunity (for example, `tackle-cosell-2jhD8b41CurTOqEsG2Soinublv3`).
This is the value returned in the `id` field of `listOpportunities` rows and in `metadata.id` on
`getOpportunity`. The cloud-provider identifier (for example, `O123456`, returned in the response
body's top-level `id` field) is **not** accepted here.

invitation_id.name: invitation_id
invitation_id.description:
The Tackle identifier for the invitation (for example,
`tackle-invitation-2sKlF3xSRGx8M724Oy3fprAX51q`). This is the value returned in the `id`
field of `listInvitations` rows and as `invitationId` on `getInvitation`. The AWS engagement
invitation identifier (for example, `oi-xABCDzzuu`) is **not** accepted here.

BadRequest.description:
Bad Request. The request was malformed or failed validation (for example, an invalid
`sortField`/`sortOrder` value, an unsupported `tackle-operation-id`, or a request body that
fails to parse as JSON).

Unauthorized.description:
Unauthorized. The request did not include valid Tackle MTM bearer credentials, or the
authenticated principal could not be resolved.

Forbidden.description:
Forbidden. The authenticated principal is not allowed to perform the requested operation
(for example, calling `createInvitation` outside of a test environment).

NotFound.description: Not Found. No resource exists at the requested path for the authenticated vendor.

Conflict.description:
Conflict. The request cannot be applied to the resource in its current state (for example,
attempting `updateDraftOpportunity` on an opportunity that is no longer in draft state, or
`createOpportunity` with a `crmId` that already maps to an existing co-sell opportunity).

example.message: Draft opportunity cannot be updated as it is not in draft state.

Locked.description:
Locked. The request was rejected because the vendor is currently in a mid-reset state
(for example, while the vendor's AWS Partner Central connection is being re-established).
Retry the request once the vendor's reset has completed.

InternalServerError.description:
Internal Server Error. An unexpected error occurred while processing the request. Response
bodies for 5xx errors may be empty.

nationalSecurity.description:
Whether the opportunity is for a national-security or government
customer that AWS Partner Central treats as restricted. Submit `Yes`
for national-security workloads (which routes the opportunity through
AWS's restricted review path) and `No` otherwise.

id.description:
The AWS Partner Central opportunity identifier (for example,
`O123456`). This is the cloud-provider identifier, not the Tackle
identifier — to look this opportunity up in Tackle, use
`metadata.id` (`tackle-cosell-...`).

opportunityTeam.description:
Partner-side contacts assigned to this opportunity. For the AWS-side
opportunity team (AWS sales reps, partner-development managers, etc.),
see `awsOpportunitySummary.opportunityTeam`.

awsOpportunitySummary.description:
The AWS Partner Central view of this opportunity, returned only after
AWS has populated cloud-side data for the record. This is the AWS-side
snapshot — including AWS-assigned engagement details, AWS opportunity
team contacts, and AWS-derived insights — and may differ from the
partner-supplied fields outside this object until AWS finishes
processing the most recent change.

catalog.description:
Which AWS Partner Central catalog this opportunity belongs to. `AWS`
is the production catalog; `Sandbox` is the AWS Partner Central
sandbox catalog used for AWS-side integration testing. Sandbox
opportunities are isolated from production data.

involvementType.description:
How AWS will be involved in this opportunity. `Co-Sell` engages an AWS
seller to actively partner on the deal; `For Visibility Only` reports
the deal to AWS without engaging an AWS seller.

involvementTypeChangeReason.description:
Reason supplied when `involvementType` is changed for this opportunity
(for example, when a `For Visibility Only` opportunity is upgraded to
`Co-Sell` after qualification, or when an opportunity's involvement
level is adjusted in response to deal changes).

closedLostReason.description:
Reason the opportunity was closed lost, when `stage` is
`Closed Lost`. Absent on opportunities still in active stages.
AWS Partner Central accepts a broad set of values here; treat
unrecognized values as opaque.

stage.description:
AWS Partner Central sales-stage value for this opportunity.
Spans the full AWS-side lifecycle from initial discovery
(`Not Started`, `In Progress`, `Prospect`) through
qualification (`Qualify`, `Engaged`), evaluation (`Technical
Validation`, `Business Validation`), to outcome (`Launched`,
`Closed Lost`, `Closed Incomplete`). The set of stages may
expand over time; treat unrecognized values as opaque.

opportunityTeam.description:
The AWS-side opportunity team. Returned as an array with one entry per
AWS principal involved.

amount.description: Stringified decimal amount; returned as a string to preserve precision.

relatedEntityIds.description: Identifiers for entities related to the opportunity, such as AWS products and solutions.

awsProducts.description: Array of AWS product identifiers associated with the opportunity.

solutions.description: Array of solution identifiers associated with the opportunity.

hubspotCrmId.description: HubSpot Deal ID to associate with this co-sell opportunity

tackleInvitationId.description:
The Tackle identifier of the invitation this opportunity was created from, when the
opportunity originated from an inbound AWS-led invitation. Absent on opportunities
that were not created from an invitation.

hubspotCrmId.description: HubSpot Deal ID associated with this co-sell opportunity

crmOrgId.description: The Salesforce organization identifier (org ID or alias) for the CRM org this opportunity's `crmId` belongs to.

salesforceSyncError.description:
Most recent Salesforce sync error message, when the last sync attempt
failed. Absent on opportunities where the last sync attempt succeeded.
salesforceSyncError.example: INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE: TackleCoSell__c: bad field names on insert/update call

archivedAt.description: Timestamp at which the opportunity was archived. Absent on non-archived opportunities.

lastCRMSyncCloud.description: Timestamp of the last CRM sync attempt to the cloud (success or failure).

lastCRMSyncCloudStatus.description:
Status of the most recent CRM-to-cloud sync attempt for this
opportunity. Common values are `success` and `failed`. Absent on
opportunities that have never been synced to the cloud.

lastCRMSyncCloudSuccessful.description: Timestamp of the last successful CRM sync to the cloud; present only when the last sync succeeded.

lastCRMSyncReceived.description: Timestamp of the last CRM sync received from the CRM (success or failure).

lastCRMSyncReceivedStatus.description:
Status of the most recent CRM-to-Tackle inbound sync for this
opportunity. Common values are `success` and `failed`. Absent on
opportunities that have never received an inbound CRM update.

lastCRMSyncReceivedChanges.description: Map of field names to their changed values from the last CRM sync received.

salesforceSyncError.description:
Most recent Salesforce sync error message, when the last sync attempt
failed. Absent on invitations where the last sync attempt succeeded.
salesforceSyncError.example: INVALID_FIELD_FOR_INSERT_UPDATE: TackleCoSell__c: bad field names on insert/update call

awsSubmission.description: This information is required to start engagement with AWS.

nationalSecurity.description:
Whether the opportunity is for a national-security or government
customer that AWS Partner Central treats as restricted. Submit `Yes`
for national-security workloads (which routes the opportunity through
AWS's restricted review path) and `No` otherwise.

enum: Co-Sell - Total Cost of Ownership Evaluation
Co-Sell - Support for Public Tender / RFx

awsMarketplaceOffers.description: Array of AWS Marketplace offer identifiers associated with the opportunity.

awsProducts.description:
Array of AWS product identifiers associated with the opportunity. These represent AWS services
or products that are part of the customer's solution (e.g., AmazonBedrock, AmazonS3, AmazonEC2Trn2).

closedLostReason.description:
Reason the opportunity was closed lost, when `stage` is
`Closed Lost`. Absent on opportunities still in active stages.

stage.description:
AWS Partner Central sales-stage value for this opportunity, restricted
to the stages used in partner-side reporting and updates. Move through
the stages in order as the deal progresses (`Prospect` → `Qualified` →
`Technical Validation` → `Business Validation` → `Committed` →
`Launched`); set to `Closed Lost` and supply `closedLostReason` if the
opportunity is lost.

targetCloseDate.description: The target close date for the opportunity, formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

source.description:
AWS Partner Central marketing source for the opportunity. Common values
include `None`, `Marketing Activity`, and `Other`; treat unrecognized
values as opaque.

apnPrograms.description:
AWS Partner Network (APN) programs associated with this opportunity,
returned as an array of program names from the enumerated list below.

enum: Customer has shown interest in solution
Agreed on solution to Business Problem

Insights.description: AWS-derived insights about the opportunity, populated by AWS Partner Central when available.

nextBestActions.description: AWS-suggested next-best-action text for the opportunity, when provided.

invitationId.description:
The Tackle ID for the invitation. Note: `getInvitation` returns this field
as `invitationId` (lowercase `d`); `createInvitation` returns the same
logical value as `invitationID` (capital `ID`). Consumers should handle both.

opportunityId.description:
The cloud-provider opportunity identifier this invitation is linked to,
when the invitation has been accepted or otherwise associated with an
opportunity. Absent on invitations that are not (yet) linked to an
opportunity.

Casing note: `getInvitation` returns this value as `opportunityId`
(lowercase `d`), while `listInvitations` rows return the same logical
value as `opportunityID` (capital `ID`). Clients should accept both
casings.

senderContacts.description:
The AWS-side contacts attached to the invitation, including the AWS
sales rep, account owner, and partner-development managers. Returned
as an array of contact records.

CreateInvitationRequest.description:
Request body for `createInvitation` (test-environment-only). The required fields are
the values consumed when constructing the simulated invitation; other fields are
optional.

senderAwsAccountID.description: The AWS account ID of the simulated sender.

expectedCustomerSpend.description:
Expected customer spend amounts associated with the invitation. Use
the documented camelCase field name `expectedCustomerSpend` — the
capital-E form `ExpectedCustomerSpend` is currently accepted as a
legacy compatibility, but new integrations should always send the
camelCase form to remain forward-compatible.

total.description: The total number of opportunities that matches the filter criteria.

currentPageCount.description: The number of opportunities returned in the current page.

isNextPage.description: A boolean value indicating if there are more opportunities to be fetched.

nextIndex.description: The starting index to use for fetching the next page of opportunities. Only present when `isNextPage` is `true`.

targetCloseDate.description: The target close date of the opportunity, formatted as `YYYY-MM-DD`.

nextIndex.description: The starting index to use for fetching the next page of invitations. Only present when `isNextPage` is `true`.

opportunityID.description:
The cloud-provider opportunity identifier this invitation is linked to, when known.
Note: `listInvitations` rows emit this field as `opportunityID` (capital `ID`), while
`getInvitation` returns the same logical value as `opportunityId` (lowercase `d`).
Consumers should handle both casings.

origin.description: The origin of the invitation. `aws` for AWS-led invitations, `partner` for partner-led.

senderCompanyName.description: The display name of the sending account. For AWS-led invitations this is `AWS`.

nextIndex.description: The starting index to use for fetching the next page of solutions. Only present when `isNextPage` is `true`.

operation.description:
The operation recorded for this history event. This is a free-form string,
intentionally not enumerated. Common values include the lifecycle operations
exposed by `createOpportunity` and the `tackle-operation-id` header on
`updateOpportunity` (for example `createOpportunity`, `createDraftOpportunity`,
`updateOpportunity`, `updateDraftOpportunity`,
`updateStartEngagementOpportunity`, `startEngagement`, `closeLostOpportunity`,
`launchOpportunity`, `updateOpportunityCRMID`, `acceptOpportunity`,
`rejectOpportunity`), plus synthetic system events such as `internalUpdateEvent`
and `cloudUpdateEvent`. History records may also include CRM-sync and
partner-system operations beyond this list; clients should treat the value as
an opaque string and surface unknown values verbatim rather than rejecting
them.

cloudRaw.description:
Raw cloud-provider snapshot associated with this history event. Present
only when the recorded event captured a non-empty cloud-side snapshot;
omitted on events without one. For AWS, this corresponds to the serialized
opportunity payload returned by AWS Partner Central at the time the event
was recorded; clients should treat the contents as opaque diagnostic data,
since the shape varies by cloud provider and operation.

cloudResponses.description:
Per-request results from AWS Partner Central for the operations recorded
in this event. On success, each entry's `response` object contains the
AWS payload and `success` is `true`. On failure, `response` is `null`,
`success` is `false`, and one of `errorType`, `errorResponse`, or
`errorResponses` is populated with the AWS error detail.

activityDetails.description:
Details about the principal that performed the operation. The full set of
principal fields (`id`, `type`, `email`, `givenName`, `familyName`,
`pictureUrl`) appears alongside `displayText`.

displayText.description: A human-readable summary of the action that produced this event.

id.description:
Identifier for the principal that performed the action.

- For events caused by a person, this is the Tackle user ID.
- For events caused by an M2M client, this is the machine principal ID.
- For system-generated events, this is one of the reserved identifiers
  `tackle-internal-update` (Tackle-initiated background updates) or
  `aws-update` (updates that originated from AWS Partner Central).

Treat any unrecognized identifier as an opaque string.

type.description:
Principal type. Common values include `user` and `otkuser` for actions taken
by a person, `machine` for actions taken by an M2M client, and
`tackle-automation` for actions taken by Tackle on the integrator's behalf
(for example, scheduled retries or background reconciliation). Additional
system-generated principal types may appear over time as new automated
sources are introduced; clients should treat any unrecognized value as an
opaque string and surface it verbatim rather than rejecting the event.

email.description: Email of the principal, when known.

operation.description:
The operation recorded for this invitation history event. This is a free-form
string, intentionally not enumerated. Common values include
`acceptInvitation`, `rejectInvitation`, and synthetic system events such as

CRM-sync and partner-system operations beyond this list; clients should treat
the value as an opaque string and surface unknown values verbatim rather than
rejecting them.

Error.description:
Error envelope returned for typed error responses. Some 4xx and 5xx responses
(such as direct `Unauthorized` and `Internal Server Error` responses) may instead
return an empty body; consumers should be tolerant of that.

message.description: A short, human-readable description of the error.
